question.value: What is the role of the asymmetric dust trap in setting the chemical composition of the HD 142527 disk, and how does it compare to IRS 48?

evidence.quote: In this work, we use archival ALMA observations of the HD 142527 disk to obtain an as large as possible molecular inventory, which allows us to investigate the possible influence of the asymmetric dust trap on the disk’s chemistry.

To further investigate the role of dust substructures in setting the disk’s chemical compositions, to investigate whether the IRS 48 disk is a special case and to obtain a unique peek into the ice composition of disks, we use ALMA archival data to investigate the chemistry of the HD 142527 disk.

analysis_steps.goal: Model 3D dust temperature structure and locate the CO snowline

method.value: Construct a 3D radiative transfer model in RADMC-3D with DIANA opacities (via OpTool), visually fitting the dereddened SED and ALMA continuum radial profile to map the 20 K midplane CO snowline

evidence.quote: We have used *RADMC-3D* (cite: RADMC3D) to create a dust radiative-transfer model (see Section 10 for a full description of our model), which allowes us to investigate the location of the snowline in more detail.

The *RADMC-3D* model has been visually fitted to both the dereddened SED (obtained from (cite: VerhoeffEA11)), using $A_V$=0.3 mag (cite: FvdM20) and the ALMA continuum radial profile. For the model we have used the standard *DIANA* opacities (cite: WoitkeEA16), implemented using *OpTool* (cite: OpTool).

claims.hypothesis: Thermal sublimation of ices at the asymmetric dust trap drives the gas-phase molecular inventory of HD 142527, similar to IRS 48.
claims.experiment: Image multiple molecular species (including CO isotopologues, HCO+, DCO+, HCN, CS, H2CO, SO, SO2, CH3OH) in archival ALMA datasets and compare their spatial distributions with the continuum dust trap.
claims.result: Molecular emission is not co-spatial with the dust trap (showing a decrement at the trap and peaking on the opposite side), and ice-sublimation tracers SO, SO2, and CH3OH are not detected (CS/SO > 1, H2CO/CH3OH >= 114).
claims.finding: Thermal sublimation of icy mantles does not play a major role in changing the gas-phase composition of the outer disk in HD 142527, because the dust trap is located much further out (~150-175 au) where temperatures are too low (~28-30 K).

evidence.quote: As the emission of the observed molecules is not co-spatial with the dust trap and no or are found, thermal sublimation of icy mantles does not appear to play a major role in changing the gas-phase composition of the outer disk in HD 142527 disk.
For disks such as HD 142527, which have dust traps at much larger radii, the temperature is too low for the sublimation of these kinds of ices, yielding higher /-ratios.

claims.hypothesis: The CO snowline in the HD 142527 disk is located beyond the radial location of the asymmetric dust trap.
claims.experiment: Extract azimuthally averaged deprojected radial profiles of optically thin 13C18O J=3-2 and DCO+ J=4-3 using GoFish, and compute a 3D dust temperature model using RADMC-3D.
claims.result: 13C18O originates from the same radial region as the continuum (~175 au) without freezing out, DCO+ peaks beyond the dust trap (~200-275 au), and the RADMC-3D 20 K midplane contour lies at ~220-280 au.
claims.finding: The CO snowline lies beyond the dust trap (at ~220-300 au).

claims.hypothesis: The observed azimuthal asymmetries in the main CO isotopologues and in HCN and CS are caused by continuum over-subtraction and shadowing by the misaligned inner disk, rather than freeze-out at the dust trap alone.
claims.experiment: Compare deprojected moment-0 maps and velocity channel maps of CO isotopologues, HCN, and CS with the continuum dust trap and scattered light shadow locations.
claims.result: Main CO isotopologues show a dip at the dust trap despite the CO snowline lying beyond the trap; HCN and CS emission encloses the dust trap and shows brightness turning-points coinciding with the northern and southern scattered light shadows.
claims.finding: Continuum over-subtraction causes the apparent decrement in the main CO isotopologues at the dust trap, while shadowing by the misaligned inner disk likely causes the azimuthal asymmetries in HCN and CS.

claims.hypothesis: The observed H2CO in HD 142527 is primarily formed via cold gas-phase reactions rather than grain-surface CO hydrogenation followed by thermal desorption.
claims.experiment: Perform a rotational diagram MCMC analysis on four H2CO transitions to measure N_tot and T_rot, and compare N(H2CO) with the 3-sigma upper limit of CH3OH.
claims.result: H2CO has T_rot = 20.1 +0.8/-0.7 K, N_tot = (2.1 +/- 0.2) x 10^14 cm^-2, and H2CO/CH3OH >= 114 +/- 14, while peaking on the opposite side of the disk from the dust trap.
claims.finding: Gaseous H2CO in HD 142527 mainly forms through cold gas-phase chemistry in the molecular layer close to the midplane, although non-thermal desorption at the dust trap cannot be ruled out.

evidence.quote: Using our observations of and and a *RADMC-3D* model, we determine the snowline to be located beyond the dust traps, favouring cold gas-phase formation of , rather than the hydrogenation of -ice and subsequent sublimation.

why_this_data.value: Archival ALMA datasets were selected to have spatial resolution sufficient to resolve the cavity and asymmetric dust trap, and to cover transitions of molecules detected in IRS 48 with E_up < 150 K and log(A_ij) > -5.

evidence.quote: The analysed datasets were selected based on the highest chance of observing transitions of , , , and , of which the latter four have been detected in the IRS 48 dust trap, allowing for proper comparisons, with upper level energies of $E_{up}<$150 K and Einstein A coefficients of $\log{A_{ij}}>$-5.

The datasets used throughout this work are summarised in Table [\[table:Datasets\]](#table:Datasets) and have the spatial resolution that is sufficiently high to resolve both the cavity and the asymmetric dust trap.

why_this_method.value: Velocity channel width of 0.5 km s^-1 was chosen for consistency across datasets; GoFish spectral stacking was used to boost SNR of weak lines; 13C18O was used for the gas mass because more common CO isotopologues are optically thick.

evidence.quote: The chosen channel width ensures consistency between the different datasets and provides sufficient velocity resolution for the aims of this work, considering that we do not investigate line kinematics.

evidence.loc: GoFish: Searching for weak line emission
evidence.quote: *GoFish* uses a spectral stacking technique, first introduced by (cite: YenEA16), which accounts for the Keplerian rotation of the disk and aims to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of weak line emission by aligning and stacking the spectra taken from different (e.g. blue- and redshifted) sides of the disk.
From this analysis, we confirm that the more common (, and ) must be optically thick and using their observations to determine the gas mass would only yield a lower limit.

As this is lower than the sublimation temperature of ($\sim$66 K (cite: PenteadoEA17)), thermal desorption of can be ruled out.

limitations_admitted.value: Low SNR of the 13C18O and DCO+ image cubes prevents constraining whether their emission (and thus the snowline location) is azimuthally asymmetric.

limitations_admitted.value: Inferring the CO snowline from DCO+ alone is non-trivial because outer DCO+ rings can also arise from non-thermal CO desorption or a midplane thermal inversion; N2H+ observations are needed to confirm.

evidence.quote: The relationship between and the CO snowline is therefore non trivial and we require observations of the preferred CO snowline tracer (cite: vtHoffEA17) to confirm our hypothesis for the HD 142527 disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Current observations lack the sensitivity to detect low-abundance products of non-thermal desorption (such as CH3OH and SO) at the dust trap.

evidence.quote: Another difference is that we do not (yet) reach the sensitivity in the HD 142527 observations to detect the products of non-thermal desorption processes.

referee_caveats_inferred: Noticeable typo in the Acknowledgements project code list (2012.1.00613.S instead of 2012.1.00631.S) and a typo in the uncertainty of HCO+ 8-7 column density in Table 1 ((1.3 +/- 9.1) x 10^14 cm^-2).

Slight discrepancy in the reported solid angle Omega for the H2CO rotational diagram between Section 3.1.3 (4.7e-11 sr, giving N_tot = 2.1e14 cm^-2) and Table 2 (4.1e-11 sr, giving N_tot = 1.6e14 cm^-2).

Using a single constant rotational temperature (T_rot = 35 K) across all molecules and radii for the disk-averaged column densities and gas mass profile introduces systematic uncertainty, especially since H2CO is measured at T_rot ~ 20 K.
Gas mass derivation relies on canonical ISM CO/H2 (10^-4) and isotopic ratios without accounting for chemical CO depletion or isotope-selective photodissociation.
